raw.details:
BioBridge – Bio Innovation Hackathon 2026 (For Biology or Bio Related Streams only)

Website: biobridge.ksrct.ac.in

Fill out this form if accomodation needed : https://forms.gle/i9Zkk6DmFnBAbccG6

Organized by:

  • K.S. Rangasamy College of Technology (KSRCT)
  • Marabanu
  • StartupTN

About BioBridge:

  • BioBridge is a bio-innovation hackathon designed to bring together students and innovators to address real-world challenges across biotechnology and allied domains.
  • Participants will work in teams to understand biological challenges, develop innovative and practical solutions, and demonstrate their potential for real-world impact.
  • The hackathon brings together biology, technology, innovation and entrepreneurship across healthcare, drug discovery, bioinformatics, agriculture, food technology, environmental biotechnology and emerging bio-innovation areas.

Hackathon Themes & Problem Statements:

BioBridge features 36 problem statements organised across seven thematic tracks. Each problem statement has a unique code that should be used when submitting the Round 1 proposal.

Theme 1: Precision Biotherapeutics & Drug Discovery:

  • BB-PB-01 | Repurposing shortlist for drug-resistant TB
  • BB-PB-02 | Protein structure and binding-site explorer
  • BB-PB-03 | Last-mile cold chain integrity for biologics
  • BB-PB-04 | AMR surveillance from hospital antibiogram data
  • BB-PB-05 | Antimicrobial peptides from regional biodiversity

Theme 2: Diagnostics & Medical Devices:

  • BB-DM-01 | Non-invasive anaemia screening
  • BB-DM-02 | Field test for water-borne pathogens
  • BB-DM-03 | Smartphone microscopy for slide screening
  • BB-DM-04 | Oral and cervical cancer triage at PHCs
  • BB-DM-05 | Monitoring for high-risk pregnancy at home

Theme 3: Bioinformatics, Genomics & Bio-AI:

  • BB-BG-01 | Variant file to a counsellor-ready report
  • BB-BG-02 | Carrier screening guidance in regional languages
  • BB-BG-03 | Biodiversity assessment from environmental DNA
  • BB-BG-04 | Pharmacogenomic dosing for Indian populations
  • BB-BG-05 | Catching hallucination in biomedical AI summaries

Theme 4: Climate-Resilient Agriculture & Agri-Biotech:

  • BB-CA-01 | Quality check for biologicals at point of sale
  • BB-CA-02 | Offline crop disease detection
  • BB-CA-03 | Microbial consortium from soil health data
  • BB-CA-04 | Verifiable traceability for organic produce
  • BB-CA-05 | Contamination early warning in tissue culture

Theme 5: Functional Foods, Nutrition & Smart Proteins:

  • BB-FN-01 | Alternative protein from a local substrate
  • BB-FN-02 | Bio-based edible coatings for perishables
  • BB-FN-03 | Rapid adulteration detection
  • BB-FN-04 | Functional food for a defined deficiency
  • BB-FN-05 | Low-cost fermentation monitoring

Theme 6: Environmental, Industrial & Waste-to-Value Biotech:

  • BB-EW-01 | Bioremediation of textile dye effluent
  • BB-EW-02 | Campus organic waste to insect protein and frass
  • BB-EW-03 | Microbial or enzymatic plastic degradation
  • BB-EW-04 | Agro-residue valorisation instead of burning
  • BB-EW-05 | Biosensor for heavy metals in groundwater

Theme 7: Open Bio Track:

  • BB-OB-01 | Biological life support for space missions
  • BB-OB-02 | Biosafety compliance in college laboratories
  • BB-OB-03 | Regulatory pathway navigator for founders
  • BB-OB-04 | Authentication of herbal raw material
  • BB-OB-05 | Virtual lab for experiments students cannot access
  • BB-OB-06 | Wildcard – Your Own Bio-Related Problem

Eligibility & Team Rules:

  • Open to UG and PG students from any discipline.
  • Teams should consist of 2–4 members.
  • Each team should register from a single college/institution.
  • Every team member must provide accurate personal and academic details.
  • Each team must designate a Team Lead as the primary point of contact.
  • Each team can work on one problem statement.
  • The selected problem statement will remain associated with the team during the subsequent stages.

Hackathon Process:

Stage 1 – Team Registration:

  • Teams register by providing their team, institution and member details.

Stage 2 – Round 1: Idea Submission:

  • Registered teams select:
  • Theme → Problem Statement
  • Teams then submit a one-page write-up describing their proposed solution.

Stage 3 – Screening & Shortlisting:

  • The submitted ideas will be reviewed by the evaluation team. The top teams will be shortlisted for the next stage.

Stage 4 – Build Phase:

  • Shortlisted teams will develop and refine their proposed solutions with mentorship and support.

Stage 5 – Pitch Deck Submission:

  • Teams will submit a pitch deck covering their solution, development progress, market/business potential and go-to-market approach, as applicable.

Stage 6 – Jury Evaluation:

  • Shortlisted teams will present their solutions to the jury.
  • Evaluation will consider:
  • Technical Feasibility
  • Business Viability
  • Impact & Sustainability
  • Clarity of Pitch

Stage 7 – Demo Day:

  • Top teams will showcase their working solutions and present their ideas live.

Stage 8 – Awards:

  • The top-performing teams will be recognised and awarded based on their overall performance.

Round 1 – Idea Submission:

Round 1 is the initial idea-screening stage of BioBridge.

Each registered team must:

  • Select one BioBridge Theme.
  • Select one Problem Statement under the chosen theme.
  • Prepare a one-page solution write-up.
  • Submit the one-pager through the designated submission platform.

Problem Statement Code:

Teams must mention the exact problem statement code in their submission.

Example: BB-PB-01

The code should correspond to the problem statement selected by the team.

One-Page Submission Format:

Each team must submit one one-page write-up using the template provided by the organisers.

File Format: PDF
Suggested Maximum File Size: 5 MB
Recommended File Name: TeamName_StatementCode.pdf

The one-page proposal should clearly communicate the team's understanding of the selected challenge and its proposed solution.

Open Bio Track – Wildcard:

Teams that wish to address a bio-related challenge that is not covered by the listed problem statements may participate under the Open Bio Track – Wildcard.

Teams must submit their own bio-related problem title along with their proposal.

The proposed problem will be reviewed by the organising team and is subject to approval.

Important Guidelines:

  • Teams must provide accurate information during registration and submission.
  • Each team should select and submit only one problem statement.
  • Teams must use the correct Problem Statement Code in their Round 1 submission.
  • The one-page submission must follow the prescribed template.
  • Submissions should clearly demonstrate the relevance of the proposed solution to the selected problem.
  • Shortlisted teams will receive further instructions regarding the build phase, mentorship, pitch deck and final presentation.
  • Teams should ensure that all submitted information and documents are complete and accurate.

BioBridge:

Bio-based Solutions for a Sustainable Tomorrow

BioBridge aims to create a platform where biology, technology, innovation and entrepreneurship come together to develop practical solutions for real-world challenges and contribute towards a more sustainable future.

  • K.S. Rangasamy College of Technology (KSRCT)
  • Marabanu
  • StartupTN
